- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next period.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has moved >3% from 10-day average, model often fails to revert; adjust forecast toward 10-day moving average within 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates late-period prices (last 5–7 days); reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is flat or declining (0.2–0.6), model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values unless sentiment turns bullish.
